doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Parents' views on his music career and his college years
summary: His mother's Adventist church-school choice over studying with David Baker, and what he learned later at Illinois.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Uh huh. Did he and your mother or your stepmother encourage you — well how did they feel about you pursuing music as a career?

Well my mother was fine with it. Actually when I was going to college Dad wanted me to go study with David Baker at IU, but my mother, because she is a Seventh Day Adventist, very church related, “No, send him to this church school.” Well he did it the first year, then the second year, by the fourth year he had kind of given up. So I kind of learned stuff on my own. I had a really good ear but actually this experience that I had at Illinois I learned more about music there than I ever learned in my life. And I wish I could have started learning that earlier, just the intricacies of improvisation, what you have to do, all the transcriptions we have to do in order to sound good, all that kind of stuff. And a lot of guys have really good ears, but everybody can’t be an intricate improviser. Some people have to work at it. You have to really study the guys, and then you’ll get your own sound eventually, but you sound like them sometimes before you get your own sound. So I’m learning that on the other end. But you know that’s okay. Life is going pretty well. Like I said I love teaching, even though I’m doing Zoom teaching. I usually buy bagels for my students every semester, I can’t buy bagels for them this time.
